title: PoC Exploit Released for Microsoft SCCM Attack Chain From Domain User to SYSTEM
content_md: A proof-of-concept exploit chain targeting Microsoft Configuration Manager (formerly SCCM) has been publicly released after being assigned the CVE-2026-47301 identifier. The research describes a path from a low-privileged domain user to SYSTEM-level code execution on a Configuration Manager Primary Site Server, potentially placing enterprise management infrastructure at risk. According to Omri Baso, the attack combines multiple weaknesses in the Configuration Manager processing workflow: broken access control, CAB archive extraction path traversal, arbitrary file write, certificate verification bypass, and DLL hijacking. Together, these issues reportedly allow an authenticated Active Directory user to place malicious files in the Configuration Manager installation directory and wait for a privileged service to load them. PoC Exploit Released for Microsoft SCCM Attack Chain The core technique relies on a specially crafted CAB archive. Rather than requiring knowledge of the SCCM installation path, the archive uses traversal sequences to write files relative to the intended extraction directory. The PoC reportedly drops two DLLs into the Configuration Manager bin\X64 directory: adsource.dll and adsource_original.dll . The second file is intended to support DLL proxying, allowing the malicious replacement DLL to preserve expected functionality while avoiding a crash of the SMS_EXECUTIVE service.
